title: Belling the Cat
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, in a cosy old farmhouse, there lived a family of little mice, tucked away behind the kitchen wall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They had everything a mouse could wish for. Warm nests, crumbs of cheese, and the sweetest seed cake. But they had one big worry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The farmhouse cat. She was big and fluffy, and very, very quiet. And whenever a mouse came out for a crumb, she would creep up, soft as a shadow... and pounce!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So one night, all the mice gathered for a meeting, by the light of a little candle.

lines.speaker: elder
lines.speech: [old, kind, a little creaky] Friends, we must find a way to keep ourselves safe from the cat. Who has an idea?
lines.text: Friends, we must find a way to keep ourselves safe from the cat. Who has an idea?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The mice whispered and wondered. Then a bright young mouse jumped up onto a cotton reel.

lines.speaker: young
lines.speech: [eager, excited] I know! Let's tie a little bell around the cat's neck!
lines.text: I know! Let's tie a little bell around the cat's neck!

lines.speaker: young
lines.speech: [proud, explaining] Then, whenever she comes near, we'll hear it go jingle, jingle, and we can all run and hide!
lines.text: Then, whenever she comes near, we'll hear it go jingle, jingle, and we can all run and hide!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What a wonderful idea! The mice cheered and clapped their tiny paws, and danced around the candle.

lines.speaker: elder
lines.speech: [gently, after a pause] It is a very good plan. But tell me, little ones...
lines.text: It is a very good plan. But tell me, little ones...

lines.speaker: elder
lines.speech: [softly, with a twinkle] Who will put the bell on the cat?
lines.text: Who will put the bell on the cat?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Suddenly, the room went very, very quiet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One mouse looked at his toes. Another looked at the ceiling. And the bright young mouse slowly sat back down.

lines.speaker: young
lines.speech: [sheepish, small voice] Oh... I didn't think of that part.
lines.text: Oh... I didn't think of that part.

lines.speaker: elder
lines.speech: [warm, wise, kindly chuckle] It is easy to have a clever idea. The hard part, my dears, is carrying it out.
lines.text: It is easy to have a clever idea. The hard part, my dears, is carrying it out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And so, the little mice decided to be extra careful, and to always stay close together.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They blew out the candle, and snuggled into their soft nests of wool and feathers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And out in the kitchen, by the warm stove, the big fluffy cat curled up too, and purred herself to sleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moon peeked in through the window, and the whole farmhouse was quiet and still.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
